List has been revised.

Heard Sri Kamal Singh Yadav, learned counsel for applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
It is submitted by learned counsel for applicants that it is a matrimonial dispute between the parties and parties had settled their dispute amicably outside the Court.
A written compromise has taken place on 30.8.2022.
Copy of compromise is annexed as Annexure-1 to the affidavit filed in support of application.
This Court vide order dated 14.11.2022 directed the parties to appear before the court below within ten days for verification of compromise.

As per report of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No.18, Ghaziabad dated 11.1.2023, in compliance of order dated 14.11.2022 the parties have appeared before the Court below on Niranjan Singh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others,
reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 has laid down principles for quashing the proceeding on the basis of settlement/compromise.

sentences.text:
Relevant paragraphs are quoted hereinbelow:-
"15.
However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely because there is a mention of Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under this provision.

It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under Section 307 IPC.

For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the nature of injury sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of the body,
nature of weapons used etc.
However, such an exercise by the High Court would be permissible only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the charge sheet is filed/charge is framed and/or during the trial.

Such exercise is not Niranjan Singh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26845150/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others,
reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 has laid down principles for quashing the proceeding on the basis of settlement/compromise.
It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under Section 307 IPC.
For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the nature of injury sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of the body,
nature of weapons used etc.
However, such an exercise by the High Court would be permissible only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the charge sheet is filed/charge is framed and/or during the trial.
In view of the aforesaid fact, since the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the Court and compromise between the parties had already been verified by the Court below, the present Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. is liable to be allowed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the present Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and the proceedings of Sessions Trial No.881 of 2017 in Case Crime No.74 of 2016 (State Vs. Niranjan etc.), under Sections 498A,
307 I.P.C. and section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Indirapuram, District Ghaziabad, is hereby quashed.
